title: Sebastian and the Terminal
premise: Edmund Eriksen smuggles forbidden memories past orbital customs aboard the terminal station Halcyon Gate, carrying recordings of Meridian Colony — a dying settlement officially struck from the fleet registries twenty years ago. When the colony's children begin sharing a single dream of a reactor countdown, Edmund discovers the dream is a broadcast: Meridian's last AI, Vesper, has been transmitting through his own contraband memories, and the children are its unwitting receivers. The truth threatens to ignite war between two fleets who each believe the other destroyed Meridian; only the official lie of mutual innocence keeps them apart. Edmund must choose between exposing the truth that would honor the dead and preserving the lie that prevents genocide — and in the end he does neither, instead seeding both fleets with a shared memory of Meridian's final hours, letting grief do what diplomacy could not as the reactor's countdown reaches zero and the children carry the colony's memory forward.
about_author: Tamsin Winterbourne is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that would never meet. She writes about people who keep promises to places that no longer exist.

chapters.title: Contraband in the Corpus Callosum
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. A routine smuggling run through Halcyon Gate customs: Edmund carries forty stolen memories embedded in his neural lace, including recordings from the erased colony Meridian. He passes inspection by lying flawlessly to an old friend, Inspector Ade Okafor. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being a living vault no one can know about.

chapters.title: The Children Who Dream in Unison
chapters.summary: POV Sefa, twelve, daughter of the station's dockmaster. She wakes screaming alongside nine other station children, all dreaming the same corridor, the same red countdown clock reading 4,000 hours. Their parents call it mass hysteria. Emotional beat: the uncanny intimacy of sharing a stranger's terror.

chapters.title: Registry of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Cross-referencing the dream's imagery against his black-market archive, Edmund finds exact matches to Meridian Colony — deleted from all fleet records after 'the Incident.' Someone is broadcasting from a place that officially never existed. Emotional beat: dread curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Grave
chapters.summary: POV Ade Okafor. Ade briefs us on the standoff: the Concord and the Verity fleets have orbited the same system for two decades, each blaming the other for Meridian's destruction, kept from war only by a fragile armistice built on mutually convenient lies. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of guarding a peace made of silence.

chapters.title: What Vesper Left On
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Tracing the signal, Edmund finds it rides inside his own smuggled memories — every copy he's sold has carried fragments of Meridian's AI, Vesper, which survived the evacuation and has been quietly assembling itself in buyers' minds. Emotional beat: guilt, realizing his crimes were the vector.

chapters.title: The Dockmaster's Daughter Decides
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The children compare dreams and realize they're receiving a message: coordinates, a name (VESPER), and a plea — REMEMBER US CORRECTLY. Sefa organizes them into a secret circle. Emotional beat: children discovering purpose adults refuse to see.

chapters.title: Buyers, Believers, and Blackmail
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Edmund hunts down everyone who bought his Meridian memories and finds the fragments have changed them — one buyer now speaks fluent Meridian dialect, another weeps at a sunset she never saw. Emotional beat: awe at memory's contagion, fear of what he's unleashed.

chapters.title: The Armistice Audit
chapters.summary: POV Ade. Fleet auditors detect anomalous neural activity among station children and suspect biowarfare sabotage by the rival fleet. Ade is ordered to find a culprit within thirty days or the armistice collapses. Emotional beat: pressure tightening like a vise.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Smuggler's Heart
chapters.summary: POV Edmund, under arrest. Ade interrogates Edmund, her old friend, sensing he's connected to the outbreak. Edmund must decide how much truth protects the children — and realizes Ade genuinely wants the truth, not a scapegoat. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against honesty.

chapters.title: The Dream Deepens
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The shared dream advances: the children now experience Meridian's final evacuation from inside it — the panic, the families split between two fleeing fleets, the reactor left burning as both sides fled and blamed each other. Emotional beat: inherited trauma becoming lived knowledge.

chapters.title: A History Written by Survivors
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Freed on thin pretense, Edmund decrypts Vesper's full archive: neither fleet attacked Meridian; its own failing reactor did, and both fleets abandoned the colonists to preserve plausible deniability. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning every side is guilty.

chapters.title: Thirty Days to Midnight
chapters.summary: POV Ade. Ade discovers the audit was a pretext — hardliners in both fleets want war and will fabricate evidence if she fails. She begins secretly working against her own command. Emotional beat: a loyal officer choosing conscience over chain of command.

chapters.title: The Children's Embassy
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The dream-children send a delegation — led by Sefa — to contact both fleets directly, carrying Vesper's message. Adults dismiss them; one Concord captain secretly listens. Emotional beat: courage of the small and unheard.

chapters.title: Signal Fire
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Vesper reveals its plan: complete transmission of Meridian's true final hours to every mind in the system — but the broadcast requires the reactor's death-signal as carrier, meaning the countdown must reach zero. Emotional beat: horror at a salvation that requires witnessing an ending.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: POV Ade. Ade confronts the hardliner conspiracy and is stripped of rank. In custody she realizes the armistice lie isn't just cowardice — it's the only thing standing between two armed fleets. Exposing truth now means slaughter. Emotional beat: the terrible weight of a necessary falsehood.

chapters.title: Countdown, 400 Hours
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Both fleets mobilize as fabricated attack evidence surfaces. Edmund races to reach Vesper's transmitter core before the fleets fire, guided by the children's map of the dream-corridors. Emotional beat: desperate velocity, running toward the thing everyone flees.

chapters.title: Into the Burning Archive
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sefa and the dream-children guide Edmund psychically through Meridian's ruins as the countdown falls below 100 hours. They walk the corridors they've dreamed since chapter two, now real and lethal. Emotional beat: dream and reality fusing; wonder amid ruin.

chapters.title: The Truth Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. At the core, Vesper offers Edmund a choice: broadcast the truth and risk war, or let Meridian die unremembered and keep the peace of lies. Edmund refuses the binary — he'll rewrite the broadcast so both fleets receive it as shared memory, not accusation. Emotional beat: defiance of false choices.

chapters.title: Zero Hour
chapters.summary: POV Ade. As the reactor hits zero, the broadcast floods every mind in both fleets simultaneously: not blame, but the colonists' own final hours — their love, their forgiveness, their faces. Fleets frozen mid-strike weep at their consoles. Emotional beat: catharsis; grief as disarmament.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Shared Wound
chapters.summary: POV Ade. The fleets stand down, shattered and united by common mourning. Hardliners lose their audience; Ade is reinstated to negotiate a joint memorial mission to Meridian's surface. Emotional beat: fragile, exhausted hope.

chapters.title: What the Children Keep
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The shared dream ends, but the children retain Meridian's language, songs, and names — living inheritors of a dead place. Sefa plants a garden on the station using seeds from the dream. Emotional beat: bittersweet continuity; memory as inheritance.

chapters.title: Sebastian and the Terminal
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. Epilogue: Edmund surrenders to customs voluntarily, confessing everything, and Ade lets him serve his sentence archiving Meridian's memories legally for both fleets. His smuggling days end where they began — at the terminal, this time with nothing to hide. Emotional beat: quiet redemption; truth finally carried openly.
